source: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR, https://osdr.nasa.gov) plant & human research, plus NASA mission reports
note: Values marked "game setting" are simulation parameters chosen for this game; everything else is a published NASA fact.

veg05.title: VEG-05 · Veggie Space Garden (ISS)
veg05.facility: Veggie plant growth unit, International Space Station

metrics.label: Grow-light spectrum
metrics.note: Red and blue light is what leaves use most for photosynthesis — that's why Veggie glows pink/purple.

metrics.label: Light intensity
metrics.note: Photon flux used for the outpost garden (game setting).

metrics.label: VEG-05 crop
metrics.note: Picked because it stays small and gives fresh fruit.

metrics.label: First space salad
metrics.note: Astronauts ate red romaine lettuce grown in Veggie (VEG-01).

veg05.why: Fresh plants give astronauts vitamins that packaged food slowly loses — and caring for a garden helps the crew feel happy far from home.

nutrition.title: Crew Nutrition & Morale

metrics.label: Daily energy need
metrics.note: Depends on the astronaut's size and how hard they work.

metrics.label: Apollo 13 water ration
metrics.note: The crew drank very little to save water for cooling the systems.

metrics.label: Apollo 13 weight loss
metrics.note: The three astronauts together lost this much in under 6 days.

nutrition.why: Without enough food and water, astronauts get tired, cold and make more mistakes — food is part of mission safety!

co2.title: Cabin Air — Oxygen & CO₂

metrics.label: CO₂ in Earth air
metrics.note: Every breath out adds more CO₂ to a small, sealed cabin.

metrics.label: Apollo 13 fix
metrics.note: Built from duct tape, plastic bags, hoses and a flight-plan cover to fit square CO₂ filters into round holes.

metrics.label: Oxygen source
metrics.note: Life support must add O₂ AND remove CO₂ at the same time.

co2.why: People breathe out carbon dioxide. In a tiny spacecraft it builds up fast, so life support has to scrub it out all day, every day.

thermal.title: Thermal Limits — Staying Warm

metrics.label: Apollo 13 cabin
metrics.note: After powering down, the Command Module got as cold as a refrigerator.

metrics.label: Mars polar night
metrics.note: Martian poles get far colder than anywhere people live on Earth (game uses −80 °C).

thermal.why: Electronics and heaters keep a spacecraft warm. Cut the power and the cold of space quickly creeps inside.

radiation.title: Space Radiation Dose

metrics.label: Mars surface dose
metrics.note: Measured by the Curiosity rover's RAD instrument.

metrics.label: Cruise to Mars
metrics.note: Measured inside Curiosity's spacecraft on the way to Mars.

metrics.label: Natural dose on Earth
metrics.note: Earth's magnetic field and thick air protect us.

radiation.why: Solar flares and particle storms shoot out tiny, super-fast particles. Shields and thick walls slow them down before they reach the crew.
